name: ios-simulator-build
description: Builds Release iOS simulator apps (clean prebuild, pinned Xcode, UDID-named simulator) and proves the .app. Use when smoke-testing on the iOS simulator, or xcodebuild, simctl or CocoaPods fails. Not for TestFlight (ios-release-testflight).

findings.excerpt: 1. **Every simulator build runs through one script and starts from a clean prebuild.** `scripts/build/build-ios-sim.ts` preflights every npm script it will run
Add `"build:ios:sim": "node scripts/build/build-ios-sim.ts"` to `package.json`, check the `.gitignore` lines (rule 12), and run `npm run typecheck`, `npx eslint
- **`APP_VARIANT=production npx expo prebuild`, then `xcodebuild` in a fresh shell.** The Constants phase and Metro see no variant; export once and keep one env
- **`npx expo start`, `npx expo run:ios` or a Debug build to "check quickly".** Metro, the dev menu and LogBox are not what users run, and `run:ios` builds on w
- **`npx expo export --clear` or deleting `$TMPDIR/metro-cache` to fix a stale variant.** It hides the missing cache key until the next build; key `cacheVersion
In JS/TS the rules read both forms: argument lists (`spawnSync('xcrun', ['simctl', 'boot', ...])`) and
or `eas` (`execSync('xcrun simctl shutdown "iPhone 17 Pro"')`), which is read like a shell line.
